chunks: And it has been narrated from Bashshār ibn Yasār, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who sells merchandise on deferred payment: may he buy it from the one to whom he sold it? He said, “Yes, there is no harm in it.”
So I said to him, “May I buy back my merchandise?” He said, “It is not your merchandise, nor your cattle, nor your sheep.”

key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: the person who possesses it or the buyer
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm or legal problem in it

ai.seo_question: Can a seller buy back merchandise that he sold on deferred payment?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling on sale transactions involving deferred payment and repurchase. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام permits buying the sold goods back from the purchaser, clarifying that once sold, the goods are no longer considered the seller’s property.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who sells merchandise for deferred payment (on credit). Can he buy it back from the one to whom he sold it?
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, there is no problem with it."

I then asked him: "Can I buy back my own merchandise?"
Imam (as) replied: "It is not your merchandise, nor your cattle, nor your sheep."
